entries.text: # change-plan
entries.reason: The skill's title heading; it holds no rule.

entries.text: Produce a plan that `/vwf:execute <folder>` can run **without you present**. That sentence is the whole bar: every decision, ruling, file scope, gate and consent the run will need is written into the folder, or the run will stop and ask for it — which defeats the point. This skill is the part that talks to the user; `/vwf:execute` is the part that does not.
entries.quote: can run with no one present

entries.text: This planner sits **beside** vwf's chain, not inside it. A blueprint slice — a flow or an entity the product describes — is `/vwf:plan` → `/vwf:execute`. A change with no blueprint slice behind it — tooling, docs, CI, a refactor, a tree the blueprint does not describe — is `/vwf:change-plan` → `/vwf:execute`. One executor runs both kinds of folder.
entries.quote: This planner sits beside vwf's chain, not inside it.

entries.text: The plan folder is the contract. `index.json` carries everything `/vwf:execute` reads mechanically, `index.md` the prose a reader needs, and the unit files what each subagent reads. Nothing lives in conversation.
entries.quote: The plan folder is the contract.

entries.text: ## Procedure
entries.reason: A section heading with no rule; the phases table replaces it.

entries.text: ### 1. Recall, then survey
entries.quote: §1 — Recall, then survey

entries.text: **Recall first.** Before asking anything, read what is already decided:
entries.quote: Before asking anything, read what is already decided

entries.text: - `docs/memory/decisions/` — any doc touching the trees the request names
entries.quote: `docs/memory/decisions/` — any doc touching the trees the request names.

entries.text: - the last plan in `docs/plans/archived/` that touched the same tree — a folder or, before 2026-09-16, a single `.md` file, the shape cycle plans had until then — reading its *Out of scope* and its *Parked* list from `index.md`, and its `gaps` list from `index.json`; an old-format folder, with an `index.md` and no `index.json`, carries all three in its `index.md`, the gaps in its *Run log* and its gaps section: the request is often one of those items coming due, and a gap the last run surfaced is a fact
entries.quote: The last plan in `docs/plans/archived/` that touched the same tree.

entries.text: - the backlog, read through `/vwf:backlog list` — the product's backlog, the prioritised list of work that cannot be picked up now, a project on the base repo's forge that the `backlog` skill alone writes. It is product-level: a session in a member repo reads the base's project, resolved from the base's remote, never one of its own. When the verb reports the backlog unreadable — `gh` absent, unauthenticated or without the `project` scope, or no project yet — record that with its reason in the facts and continue with nothing. The request is often one of its items; note every id it covers, and for each whether this plan finishes the item or lands one piece of it — interview item 2a settles it — so the plan's `index.json` can carry them on the right list. A `Bnn` id in `$ARGUMENTS` — `/vwf:backlog next` prints the launch line with it — is always one of them, and is never dropped for a weaker match. Every id noted here is a **source** id, recorded on the `index.json` `source` list, so the executor can tell a plan made for an item from one made for none. The same read tells the interview which items share the plan's priority — what §8's check counts before it recommends `/vwf:execute`. Reading the backlog is this skill's business; editing it never is — `/vwf:backlog` is its sole writer

- the base repo's `docs/plans/index.json` — the plan index, the one file where every active plan of either kind, cycle and change, its status and its priority live, read with `node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/plan-management/scripts/plan.mjs get docs/plans/index.json plans`; `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/plan-management/references/plan-index.md` is the shape, and `plan-management` its only writer. Like the backlog it is the base's alone, read from a member repo and never duplicated there. The `priority` key of the rows a new plan will require — rows of either kind — is what §5's derived priority stands on. A row whose `gaps.open` is above `0` is a landed plan with gaps that no plan took yet; a request that takes them puts its folder on `gaps_of` — interview item 2b. Reading the file is this skill's business; editing it never is — §8's `plan-management add` appends the row
entries.quote: The base repo's `docs/plans/index.json` — the plan index

entries.text: - the `docs/memory/decisions/` and `docs/memory/gaps/` folders, read by the recall rule of `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/assets/memory.md` — do not restate it here; **skip silently** when a folder is absent
entries.quote: Skip silently when a folder is absent.

entries.text: A standing decision the request contradicts is a **reversal** — name it as one in the interview, never as a fresh choice.
entries.quote: A standing decision the request contradicts is a **reversal**.

entries.text: **Survey second.** Dispatch **Explore** subagents (one message, concurrent) to map, for the request in `$ARGUMENTS`:
entries.quote: Dispatch **Explore** subagents, concurrently in one message, to map for the request:

entries.text: - the trees the change touches, and which project each belongs to — read the project registry `docs/blueprint/registry.yaml` when the repo has one, else take the repo's own top-level directories as the projects
entries.quote: The trees the change touches, and the project of each.

entries.text: - the gates that already cover those trees — the task runner's task list (`mise tasks`), the `harness:` stamp in `.config/vwf.yaml` when one is stamped (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/assets/harness.md` is the vocabulary), and the CI workflow files
entries.quote: The gates that already cover those trees

entries.text: - the docs that describe the current behaviour — the README, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/`, and any per-project README or home doc
entries.quote: The docs that describe the current behaviour

entries.text: - the third-party dependencies already available to each tree, so a unit can be told to reuse before adding
entries.quote: The third-party dependencies each tree already has

entries.text: - the repo's commit convention — `.config/git-conventional-commits.yaml` where the repo has one, else whatever its commit-message gate reads — so every unit file's `## Commit` line carries a type, and a scope, that gate accepts. A repo with no convention file takes git-workflow's common types: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `revert`, `test`, `ops`, `docs`, `merge`, `wip`
entries.quote: The repo's commit convention:

entries.text: - when the request retires or renames a name, the name itself, grepped across every tree the repo has — `.claude/`, `installer/`, `site/src/content/docs/`, `plugins/`, the root docs. Every hit is a passage the change falsifies, and every one needs an owner in some unit's `owns` before the plan is written; the three plans that skipped this each left the docs unit inheriting nobody-owned passages at run time
entries.quote: When the request retires or renames a name

entries.text: Instruct every Explore agent to return **conclusions and `file:line` pointers only** — never file contents, diffs or directory dumps. Hold the findings; they ground the questions and become the plan's facts section. Do not read the files yourself — the survey exists so the orchestrator context stays small, and the same rule binds `/vwf:execute`.
entries.quote: conclusions and `file:line` pointers only

entries.text: ### 2. Scope check
entries.quote: §2 — Scope check

entries.text: If the request is really **several independent pieces** — two trees with no shared ruling, a doctrine change plus an unrelated tooling fix — say so before refining anything. Decompose it, agree the order, and plan **one folder per piece**, each through this whole procedure. A later piece that stands on an earlier one names it in its `index.json` `requires` list; `/vwf:execute` halts until every required plan reads `COMPLETE`. One plan never swallows another. The pieces are planned one after another in this session: each runs §3 to §8, and §8's ending for a piece that is not the last goes straight back to §3 for the next piece — no launch block until the last one is planned.
entries.quote: When the request is really several independent pieces

entries.text: An answer mid-interview that raises something outside this plan's scope is **parked, durably**: acknowledge it, write it to the *Parked* list of the plan's `index.md` with enough to pick it up later, and do not widen the plan. Parked items are the first thing the next plan's recall reads. A Parked entry that belongs to a backlog item begins with its id — `- Bnn: <piece>` — and a plan that lands one piece of an item writes what remains that way, at least one line per `backlog_pieces` id, naming the chained folder where one already covers the piece.
entries.quote: An answer mid-interview that raises something outside this plan's scope is parked durably.

entries.text: ### 3. Interview, one question at a time
entries.quote: §3 — Interview, one question at a time

entries.text: Work through the checklist in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/assets/plan-interview.md` top to bottom — it is shared with `/vwf:plan`; where an item carries a *Change plans:* note, follow that note. Each item is one `AskUserQuestion` call, or a prose question when the answer is open-ended. **Never batch** — one decision per turn, and never assume one. An item the survey already answered is confirmed in a sentence, not re-asked.
entries.quote: Work through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/assets/plan-interview.md` top to bottom.

entries.text: Ask only what has **more than one reasonable answer** given the repo. Where that holds, **propose two or three approaches with their trade-offs**, lead with your recommendation and why, and let the user pick or redirect. A ruling recorded without its rejected alternatives is a ruling the next plan re-opens.
entries.quote: Ask only what has more than one reasonable answer given the repo.

entries.text: The interview is done when every checklist item has an answer recorded, and not before. If the user says "just decide", record the decision as an assumed decision with your reasoning and the alternative you rejected — the `decisions` list of `index.json` is what they review.
entries.quote: it owns the items, their order and the ending condition

entries.text: ### 4. Agree the gate and the after-landing steps, derive the release levels
entries.quote: §4 — Gates, after landing, release levels

entries.text: Four sub-steps. (a), (b) and (d) are proposed from the survey and confirmed by the user; (c) is derived and stated, never confirmed here — the user changes a level at the §5 gate. All four are written into `index.json`, and `/vwf:execute` runs **what is written and nothing it infers**.
entries.quote: Four sub-steps. Propose (a), (b) and (d) from the survey

entries.text: **(a) The three gates.** Propose the exact commands the run must pass, one per line, for each of three tiers, drawn from the survey's gate list — the repo's own task runner tasks, the capabilities the `harness:` stamp records, the checks CI already runs over the touched trees. Confirm them. They become the `gates.unit` list of `index.json`, which `/vwf:execute` runs once before each unit's commit; its `gates.wave` list, run once before wave 1 and after every wave; and its `gates.plan` list, run once over the finished tree. When the repo's `mise tasks ls` lists them, the default proposal is `mise x -- mise run code:format` for the unit gate, `mise x -- mise run code:lint` for the wave gate and `mise x -- mise run code:precommit --all` for the plan gate: the cheap check runs most often, and the full hook pass runs once. The plan gate takes `--all` because it runs over the finished, committed tree — without it, `code:precommit` checks only uncommitted files, and on a clean tree it checks nothing. A check that runs the whole hook pass or a slow test suite belongs in the plan gate, not in the wave gate. A check that only holds once a particular unit has landed is **not** a wave-gate line — the gate runs before wave 1 and must be green then — it is that unit's *Verification*, repeated in the gates unit's. A repo with no task runner and no harness stamp records `none` — say plainly, in that case, that the run has no automated gate and the wave review is the only check. The wave review is the only review a change plan runs by default: a `review` unit is written only when the change lands runnable code (item 10a), with its reason in the `decisions` list. Over a change plan's `edit` units it runs `/security-review` and the security reviewer alone — the wave review has already judged the units against their files.
entries.quote: Propose the exact commands the run must pass, one per line, for each tier.

entries.text: **(b) After landing.** Propose the ordered steps that follow a consented landing, and confirm each. Each step is confirmed at the interview (item 17) as `run` or dropped, and `run` is written to the `after_landing` list: a `run` step runs on a green landing without a prompt. A plan never carries a release step — a release is always a later hand step, `/release`. A step the user wants to check first is dropped and run by hand later; the executor never stops before a step to ask. A command already in `.config/vwf.yaml`'s `after_landing:` list is not proposed: `/vwf:execute` runs it after every green landing. Where a step stages something the session already loaded, say plainly that it is picked up only by a **restarted** session.
entries.quote: walk them by interview item 17

entries.text: Empty is a valid answer. These become the `after_landing` list of `index.json`, `[]` when empty.
entries.quote: empty is a valid answer, written `[]`

entries.text: **(c) Release levels.** For each project the units touch, derive its level from the change — never ask it (interview item 18 is stated, as item 12's priority is): breaks users → `MAJOR`, new behaviour → `MINOR`, a fix → `PATCH`, no user-visible change → `NONE`. Give each a one-line reason, and write them as the `release_levels` list of `index.json` — one entry per project the units touch, `NONE` included, each `{id, level, reason}` with the project name as its `id`.
entries.quote: Derive a level for each project the units touch, never ask it

entries.text: No unit bumps a version and no plan releases. `/vwf:execute` raises each level in `.config/releases.yaml` at landing — one key per project, the highest level wins — and `/release` is a later hand step that reads that file.
entries.quote: No unit bumps a version and no plan releases.

entries.text: **(d) Ending an `all` run.** Write `consent.end_all_run`, the answer to End an `all` run after landing (interview item 18a). Ask it only when the units' `owns` include a plugin the run itself loads — one installed in the session that runs `/vwf:execute all`, which keeps running the stale copy until it restarts; on yes, `all` ends after this plan and reports "restart, then `/vwf:execute all`". When the plan touches no such plugin, write `false` unasked.
entries.quote: Write `consent.end_all_run`, the answer to interview item 18a.

entries.text: ### 5. Present the shape — the hard gate
entries.quote: Present the shape: the hard gate

entries.text: **Nothing is written to disk before this gate.** Present, in sections scaled to their weight and confirmed one at a time:
entries.quote: Write nothing to disk before this gate.

entries.text: 1. the goal and the reversals, if any
entries.quote: The goal and the reversals, if any.

entries.text: 2. the assumed decisions — every ruling, its rejected alternatives
3. the unit map — id, wave, owned paths, depends-on — why each wave is safe to run concurrently, and the named reason each unit in a later wave waits
entries.quote: The unit map: id, wave, owned paths, depends-on.

entries.text: 4. every new third-party dependency any unit introduces: package, what for, which unit. The gate is where the user consents to a dependency; a unit never adds one the plan does not name
entries.quote: Every new third-party dependency any unit introduces

entries.text: 5. the unit gate, the wave gate, the plan gate, the after-landing steps, the gates the orchestrator keeps — and the **derived priority**, what `plan-management priority <requires…>` returns — passed the `requires` entries item 12 settled, folder basenames or none, since no folder exists before §6 — stated as a fact with the arithmetic that produced it: `10 + max` over the `priority` of every unarchived `requires` row in the plan index, naming the row it stands on, or "requires nothing active → 10". It is never asked; the one thing that changes it is a required plan the user names here that the interview missed — then the verb is run again
entries.quote: **The derived priority** is what `plan-management priority <requires…>` returns.

entries.text: 6. the consent — the End an `all` run after landing answer among it — and the release levels, each with its reason, stated as a fact like the priority; the user may change a level here
entries.quote: The consent, with the End an `all` run after landing answer among it

entries.text: 7. the parked list
entries.quote: The parked list.

entries.text: Then ask once: **approve**, **revise** or **abandon**. Revise loops back to the section named. Abandon ends here with nothing on disk and a one-line note of what was decided, so the next attempt can recall it. Only approve continues.
entries.quote: Then ask once: **approve**, **revise** or **abandon**.

entries.text: ### 6. Write the folder
entries.quote: §6 — Write the folder

entries.text: `docs/plans/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<kebab-name>/` from the template in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/assets/templates/plan-folder.md` — the one folder shape both planners write: `index.json`, `index.md` and one `NN-<unit>.md` per unit.
entries.quote: Write `docs/plans/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<kebab-name>/` from

entries.text: - **`index.json`** holds every structured fact of the plan — the keys the template names, in its order, each required, cycle-only keys aside. Write it **once**, whole, with the Write tool, then run `node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/plan-management/scripts/plan.mjs validate <folder>/index.json` — the Write and its validate are one step, the creation. A red validate means the creation is not finished: correct the content and Write the whole file again, then validate again, until it prints `<folder>/index.json: valid` — `set` refuses to write a file that does not validate, and no Edit touches `index.json`. From that first green validate on, every change to it, the self-review's fixes included, is one `plan.mjs set`, `append`, `remove` or `rewave` call; never an Edit, never a whole-file rewrite. To move units between waves — a split or a merge of waves, from the self-review or the rulings review — use one `plan.mjs rewave <file> <unit>=<wave>...` call, which rebuilds `waves` with it; when a unit moves above wave 1, first `set` its `waits`, then `rewave`. `/vwf:execute` reads and writes it with the same script. `status.state` is written `DRAFT`, with `status.detail` `DRAFT <date>`; `run` is `{}`; each unit's `status` is `pending`, with `started`, `ended` and `commit` `""` and `rounds` `0`; `waves` has one `pending` entry per wave, `W1` up to the highest unit `wave`, its `started` and `ended` `""`; each of the four `stages` is `pending` with empty times; and `gaps` and `overrides` are `[]`.
entries.quote: every `index.json` key and its initial value, the creation rule

entries.text: - **`index.md`** holds the prose only, in the template's sections: the goal and the reversals, the facts the survey established, Out of scope and Parked. It has no frontmatter, no table `/vwf:execute` reads, and no Run log.
entries.quote: **`index.md`:** write the template's sections, for the prose only.

entries.text: - **Each unit file** starts with its H1, `# U<n> — <title>`, the same text as the unit's `title` in `index.json`, and carries no header lines: its wave, kind, model, owns and depends-on live in its `units` entry alone.
entries.quote: and the unit file shape

entries.text: `type` is `vwf-change-plan`, and the cycle-only keys — `covers`, `exposure`, `acceptance` and `consent.lsp` — are absent; `validate` fails a change plan that carries one. `index.json` carries three lists of the `Bnn` ids recalled in §1, each possibly empty, written `[]`: `source` names every item this plan was made for, and each of them also sits on one of the other two; `backlog` names the items this plan **finishes** — landing sets them `Done` — and `backlog_pieces` the items it lands **one piece of** — landing sets them `Partially done`. No id sits on both. The last plan of a chain moves the id to `backlog`. `source` is empty only when no backlog item asked for the plan — work the user brought that the backlog does not hold. A fourth list, `gaps_of`, names the landed plan folders whose gaps this plan takes — interview item 2b — and is `[]` otherwise.
entries.quote: **`type`** is `vwf-change-plan`. Omit the cycle-only keys

entries.text: Rules the plan must obey, learned from the plans that came before:
entries.quote: These rules come from the plans that came before.

entries.text: - **One unit, one subagent, one commit.** A unit is stateless and inherits no context; its file carries its ruling quoted from the `decisions` list, its verification, and its commit line; its owned paths are its `owns` entry, which `/vwf:execute` puts into the dispatch prompt.
entries.quote: **One unit, one subagent, one commit**

entries.text: - **Every unit is `kind` `edit`.** A change plan has no code unit in this release. `/vwf:execute` reads each unit's `kind` from the `units` list: it dispatches the `edit` units of a wave together, in one message, and judges them by the wave review — the only check, by default. A `review` unit (`owns` `[]`, `depends_on` the units it covers, a `range` of `{"from": "", "to": ""}`, a `NN-review.md` in the template's shape) is added only when the change lands runnable code — anything that executes rather than is read: shipped shell or hook scripts, build or tooling source, an installable package — and the reason is an entry in the `decisions` list. The unit sits in a wave strictly later than every unit it covers — in the same wave it runs before their commit and reviews nothing, since it scopes by commit range — and covers, directly or transitively through `depends_on`, **every** unit in an earlier wave that no earlier review unit covers, the units that land that code and every other `edit` unit alike, since it reviews the whole range since the previous review and a finding on a unit it left out would be routed there anyway — the one rule, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/execute/references/review-unit.md`'s. Its `depends_on` names at least one unit it covers — never `[]`: a review that covers nothing reviews nothing. Preflight refuses a review unit in the wave of a unit it covers, one that covers nothing, and one that leaves an earlier unit no earlier review covers out. The `index.md` sections the template marks *cycle plans only* — Slice — and the cycle-only keys of `index.json` are omitted.
entries.quote: **Every unit is `kind` `edit`**

entries.text: - **A unit deletes with plain `rm`, never `git rm`.** A unit stages nothing, so no unit's deletion can ride another unit's commit.
entries.quote: **A unit deletes with plain `rm`, never `git rm`**

entries.text: - **Fewest waves.** Every unit sits in wave 1 unless it has a named reason to wait: it edits a path an earlier unit creates or moves, or its Verification needs an earlier unit's output. A unit that only reads the same files, or edits a neighbour of another unit's files, shares the wave. Each unit in a later wave states its reason in its `waits` key — the edit units of one wave run at once, so each needless wave is a serial step the run pays for. The fixed final units and a `review` unit keep their own waves, and their `waits` may be `""`; every other unit in wave 1 has `waits` `""`.
entries.quote: **Fewest waves** — the edit units of one wave run at once

entries.text: - **Shared-file rule.** Any file two units would write is owned by exactly one, or by the orchestrator — an entry of the `shared_files` list, its `owner` a unit id or the orchestrator. Version files are nobody's — the release task bumps them; generated files and every doc are always the orchestrator's or the final units'. Units in one wave own disjoint paths.
entries.quote: **Shared-file rule** — any file two units would write is owned by exactly one

entries.text: - **Gate deltas are units.** A change that needs a new or altered check, test, or task plans that as an owned edit, never as "update the gates".
entries.quote: **Gate deltas are units**

entries.text: - **`requires` names a folder by its basename.** A required plan is written as its `docs/plans/<date>-<name>` path as planned, and is matched — by `/vwf:execute` and by the plan index — on the basename alone, so the line is never re-pointed when the folder moves to `docs/plans/archived/`.
entries.quote: **`requires` names a folder by its basename**

entries.text: - **The two last units are fixed:** the **docs unit**, which runs `vwf:docs-sync` over the run's branch delta (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/docs-sync/SKILL.md`) and applies its findings plus every `DOCS FALSIFIED:` line the earlier units returned; and the **gates unit**, `NN-gates.md`, which runs the generators the plan names and passes the full wave gate. Nothing else touches docs; no unit bumps a version.
entries.quote: **The two last units are fixed**

entries.text: - **Assumed decisions are the `decisions` list**, one entry per ruling you made — `decision`, `ruling`, the alternative `rejected`, and the `units` it changes. It is the review surface.

- **Out of scope and Parked are explicit** sections of `index.md`. What the user declined, with the reason, and what was raised and deferred, so `/vwf:execute` never "helpfully" picks either up. What remains of a `backlog_pieces` item is a `- Bnn: <piece>` Parked line, at least one per id; a `backlog` id has none, and `plan.mjs validate` and the executor's preflight both refuse a folder that breaks either rule.
entries.quote: **Out of scope and Parked are explicit `index.md` sections**

entries.text: ### 7. Self-review
entries.quote: §7 — Self-review

entries.text: Re-read the folder with fresh eyes before handing it off, and fix inline — a wave change is one `plan.mjs rewave` call, after a `set` of each moved unit's `waits` first when it moves above wave 1. First run `node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/plan-management/scripts/plan.mjs validate <folder>/index.json`; a red result is fixed before any other check — each finding names the path that broke. It already checks the shape: every required key and enum value, unique ids, each unit's `file` present, `depends_on` naming an earlier wave, `waits` where a later wave needs it, the `review` unit's shape, and the `backlog`, `backlog_pieces` and `source` rules against the `- Bnn:` Parked lines of `index.md`. Then:
entries.quote: Re-read the folder with fresh eyes before handing it off, and fix inline.

entries.text: - every entry of the `decisions` list is **quoted** in the unit file of each id its `units` names — a ruling no unit carries is a ruling the run re-derives
entries.quote: Every entry of the `decisions` list is quoted

entries.text: - every owned path appears in exactly one unit's `owns` per wave, and every `shared_files` entry has an `owner`
entries.quote: Every owned path appears in exactly one unit's `owns` per wave

entries.text: - every unit in a wave after wave 1 — the fixed final units and a `review` unit aside — names a real reason to wait in its `waits`
entries.quote: names a real reason to wait in its `waits`

entries.text: - every gate delta from the interview is an owned edit somewhere
entries.quote: Every gate delta from the interview is an owned edit somewhere.

entries.text: - a `review` unit, when present, names its reason in the `decisions` list, covers — directly or transitively — every unit in an earlier wave that no earlier review unit covers, and sits in a wave strictly later than each of them
entries.quote: A `review` unit, when present, names its reason in the `decisions` list.

entries.text: - every unit's *Verification* names at least one gate line it must pass — a `review` unit has none, by shape
entries.quote: Every unit's *Verification* names at least one gate line it must pass.

entries.text: - every hit of the retired-name grep sits inside some unit's `owns`, and every `## Commit` line's type is one the repo's convention file allows
entries.quote: Every hit of the retired-name grep sits inside some unit's `owns`.

entries.text: - every `requires` entry resolves to a row or an archived folder, and none is `DRAFT` — invoke `plan-management resolve <folder>` and treat an *unresolvable* entry as a finding
entries.quote: Every `requires` entry resolves to a row or an archived folder

entries.text: - every id §1 noted is on `source` — a folder made for a backlog item with `backlog` and `backlog_pieces` both empty is not approved
entries.quote: Every id §1 noted is on `source`.

entries.text: - no `gaps_of` entry names a row of the plan index that is not `COMPLETE`, or whose `gaps` is `null` or has `open` `0`
entries.quote: No `gaps_of` entry names a row of the plan index that is not `COMPLETE`

entries.text: - the derived priority equals what `plan-management priority <folder>` returns
entries.quote: The derived priority equals what `plan-management priority <folder>` returns.

entries.text: - every project the units touch has a `release_levels` entry with a reason, and `consent` has no release key
entries.quote: Every project the units touch has a `release_levels` entry with a reason

entries.text: - every `consent` key carries an answer, and no `after_landing` entry carries a `mode` other than `run` — `/vwf:execute` asks nothing at run time
entries.quote: Every `consent` key carries an answer

entries.text: - the launch line names this folder
entries.quote: The launch line names this folder.

entries.text: Then the **rulings review**, item 20 of `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/assets/plan-interview.md`: a fresh `plan-rulings-reviewer` over the `DRAFT` folder, each gap it returns asked of the user one at a time and written into the folder, looped until `NO GAPS`, four rounds at most. These are the last questions the plan gets — `/vwf:execute` asks none.
entries.quote: Then run item 20 of `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/assets/plan-interview.md`

entries.text: ### 8. Hand off
entries.quote: §8 — Hand off

entries.text: In this order.
entries.quote: Run these in order.

entries.text: 1. **Hand the folder to `plan-management`.** Invoke `plan-management add <folder>` — its `add` verb sets the folder's `status` to `APPROVED` with the date (until then it is `DRAFT` and `/vwf:execute` refuses it) and appends the folder's row to the plan index — the `plans` list of the base repo's `docs/plans/index.json` — `kind` `change`, deriving the priority itself (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/plan-management/references/plan-index.md` is the shape). That skill edits the `status` key and the index; this one never does. `add` refuses while the base repo's `docs/plans/index.md` exists — the old plan format — and prints the migration message. Then stop here: the folder stays `DRAFT` and uncommitted, nothing below runs, and the output is the refusal as `add` printed it.
entries.quote: Hand the folder to `plan-management`.

entries.text: 2. **Mark the backlog items planned.** When the `backlog` or `backlog_pieces` list of `index.json` names ids, invoke `/vwf:backlog planned <ids> <folder>` with the ids of both lists — that skill edits the project, not a file; this one never does either.
entries.quote: Mark the backlog items planned.

entries.text: 3. **Commit and push the folder** through `vwf:git-workflow`, invoked with these declared preferences, so it asks nothing:
entries.quote: Commit and push the folder** through `vwf:git-workflow`.

entries.text: - **work in place on the current branch, no worktree** — its Step 1 "if declined" path. Say why: the run's worktree is cut from the integration branch, so it can see the folder only once the folder is committed there; a folder still untracked at hand-off gets swept into some later wave's commit. The index row rides the same commit for the same reason — it is a direct commit on the branch, never a worktree's
entries.quote: Work in place on the current branch, no worktree

entries.text: - **stage exactly the plan folder** and `docs/plans/index.json`, and nothing else — the `plan-management` edit rides this commit and that skill never commits; step 2 changed nothing in the tree
entries.quote: **Stage exactly the plan folder** and `docs/plans/index.json`, and nothing else.

entries.text: - **commit** with type `docs` and the message `docs: change plan — <name> — approved, awaiting execution`
entries.quote: `docs: change plan — <name> — approved, awaiting execution`

entries.text: - **push to the branch's upstream** after the commit, setting the upstream when the branch has none. The approve in §5 is the explicit request git-workflow's push rule wants; do not ask again
entries.quote: **Push to the branch's upstream** after the commit

entries.text: Then **check that nothing at this priority is left to plan**, before recommending a run. An **open** backlog item is `Backlog`, `In progress` or `Partially done`; an **unplanned** one is `Backlog`, or `Partially done` with no `Planned in:` line. The **check priority** is the highest priority among the `backlog` and `backlog_pieces` ids of `index.json`, or, when both are empty, the highest priority that has an open item. Invoke `/vwf:backlog unplanned <priority>` — with no argument when the plan names no id — and count, beside what it lists, the pieces of this session's request not yet planned (§2's split). Then end in exactly one of three ways:
entries.quote: Run this before recommending a run.

entries.text: - **Nothing unplanned** — end with the launch block below, exactly as written.
entries.quote: **Nothing unplanned** — end with the launch block below, exactly as written.

entries.text: - **Something unplanned** — no launch block. Print the unplanned pieces of this request first, then the unplanned items at the check priority, then the command for the next one — `/vwf:change-plan <item>`, or `/vwf:plan <slice>` when the item names a blueprint slice — and nothing after it. A piece of this request that is next goes straight back to §3 instead. `/vwf:execute` is unchanged; the user may still run it.
entries.quote: **Something unplanned** — no launch block.

entries.text: - **The backlog unreadable** — the verb says so; end with the launch block, preceded by one line saying the backlog could not be read, so the check did not run.
entries.quote: **The backlog unreadable** — the verb says so.

entries.text: The launch block, with nothing after it:
entries.quote: The launch block, with nothing after it:

entries.text:
```text
Run in a fresh context — a fresh session, or a runner that `all` dispatches:

/vwf:execute docs/plans/<date>-<name>

or let the queue pick it, by priority:

/vwf:execute next

or run every runnable plan, highest priority first:

/vwf:execute all
```
entries.quote:
```text
Run in a fresh context — a fresh session, or a runner that `all` dispatches:

/vwf:execute docs/plans/<date>-<name>

or let the queue pick it, by priority:

/vwf:execute next

or run every runnable plan, highest priority first:

/vwf:execute all
```

entries.text: Do not start executing. The fresh context is the point — this session's context is the survey and the interview, and the run should carry none of it.
## What this skill never does
entries.reason: A section heading with no rule; each list item under it is its own entry.

entries.text: - Writes anything to disk before the hard gate in §5 is approved
entries.quote: Write to disk before §5's approve

entries.text: - Executes a unit, edits a file the plan names, or bumps a version
- Asks two things in one turn, or asks what the repo already answers
entries.quote: one decision per turn

entries.text: - Records a landing consent it did not explicitly ask for, or a release step
entries.quote: Record only a landing consent you explicitly asked for

entries.text: - Writes a plan whose unit prompts depend on this conversation
entries.quote: Write a unit prompt that depends on this conversation

entries.text: - Pushes anywhere but the branch it stands on, and merges nothing
entries.quote: Push nowhere but the branch you stand on, and merge nothing.

entries.text: - Edits the backlog itself — it calls `/vwf:backlog`, which owns the project
entries.quote: Edit the backlog; call `/vwf:backlog`

entries.text: - Edits the plan index, `docs/plans/index.json`, or a folder's `status` key itself — `add` is the one `plan-management` verb it calls on them; every later status is `/vwf:execute`'s to call, and the archive move is the same skill's
